calls.head: Strength vs. Strength
calls.body: The Blues are the league’s best for chance quality, but the Avalanche are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Blues’ chance quality wins out.
calls.call: The Blues’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Avalanche.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Avalanche cruise past the Blues
paras: Cale Makar struck first for the Avalanche early in the first, and Martin Nečas made it 2-0 midway through the period. The Avalanche took over in the second: Josh Manson scored, Artturi Lehkonen scored, Nicolas Roy scored, and Nečas scored his second of the night to make it 6-0. Dalibor Dvorský got the Blues on the board early in the third, far too late to matter. Two players had three-point nights: Nathan MacKinnon with three assists, and Nečas with two goals and an assist.

The Avalanche drove the play, outshooting the Blues 36-26, and the scoreboard caught up. Mackenzie Blackwood made 25 saves for the Avs, and Jordan Binnington allowed six goals on 36 shots. The Avalanche moved to 2-0-0, tied for first in the NHL in points percentage, while the Blues dropped to 1-1-0, giving up the best points percentage in the NHL to the Avalanche.

items.text: The Avalanche’s Gabriel Landeskog played his 800th NHL game and had an assist.
